'''Bascom Sine Deaver Jr.''' (born August 16, 1930, in [[Macon, Georgia]])<ref name="deaver-date">{{cite journal |title=Fixed-tuned submillimeter wavelength waveguide mixers using planar Schottky-barrier diodes |journal=IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques |author2=Hesler, J.L.|author3=Hall, W.R.|author4=Crowe, T.W.|author5=Weikle R.M., II|author6=Deaver B.S., Jr|author7=Bradley, R.F.|author8= Shing-Kuo Pan |volume=45 |issue=5 |date=May 1997 |pages=653–658 |doi=10.1109/22.575581 |author=Hesler, J.L.|bibcode = 1997ITMTT..45..653H }}</ref> is a retired American physicist known for his research into [[superconductor]] applications, and a professor and assistant chairman for undergraduate studies of the [[physics]] department at the [[University of Virginia]].<!-- is this still true?
 -->

A leading researcher in the field of superconductors, he is noted for his discovery that the [[magnetic flux]] threading a superconducting ring is [[magnetic flux quantum|quantized]], a foundational discovery that led to the development of [[SQUID|superconducting quantum interference devices]], superconducting [[magnetometer]]s, and superconducting [[tunnel diode|tunnel junction diodes]] for use in [[microwave]] receivers.<ref name="fairbank">{{cite web|url=http://histsoc.stanford.edu/pdfmem/FairbankW.pdf |title=Memorial Resolution: William Martin Fairbank (1917-1989) |accessdate=2008-06-10 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070609211847/http://histsoc.stanford.edu/pdfmem/FairbankW.pdf |archivedate=2007-06-09 }}</ref> As a professor, Deaver has overseen 26 Ph.D. students, developed two undergraduate concentrations in [[optics]] and [[computational physics]], and created a B.A. degree for students {{Em dash}} a program designed to "expose students to the intellectual beauty of physics without sophisticated mathematics."<ref name="deaver-accomplishments">{{cite web |url=https://www.phys.virginia.edu/Announcements/DeaverFund/DeaverAccomplishments.pdf |title=Summary of Accomplishments: Bascom S. Deaver, Jr. |publisher=[[University of Virginia]]|accessdate=2008-06-06}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Deaver received his undergraduate B.S. degree from the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] in 1952, and his masters at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1954.

Between 1954 and 1957, he was a physicist and commissioned a lieutenant in the [[United States Air Force]] at the [[Air Force Special Weapons Center]] at [[Kirtland Air Force Base]] in [[New Mexico]]. Deaver began his career as a professor at the University of Virginia in 1965, having completed in 1962 his PhD at [[Stanford University]], under the supervision of [[William M. Fairbank]], with thesis ''Experimental evidence for quantized magnetic flux in superconducting cylinders''. He attended the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as an [[Sloan Fellows|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]] between 1966 and 1968.<ref name="deaver-accomplishments" />

Deaver has received a number of awards at the university, including the Alumni Association's Distinguished Professor Award for teaching in 2004.<ref name="2004-award">{{cite news|url=http://www.virginia.edu/insideuva/2004/08/teaching_awards.html |title=2004 University of Virginia Teaching Awards |work=Inside UVA |last=Brickhouse |first=Robert |date=2004-04-23 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080723233843/http://www.virginia.edu/insideuva/2004/08/teaching_awards.html |archivedate=2008-07-23 }}</ref> He is a member of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Virginia Academy of Science]], the [[Raven Society]], [[Sigma Xi]], [[Tau Beta Pi]], [[Sigma Pi Sigma]], and [[Omicron Delta Kappa]]. In 2000 he received the [[George B. Pegram]] Award, for "Excellence in the Teaching of Physics in the Southeast", from the Southeastern Section of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="pegram">{{cite web |url=http://www.aps.org/units/sesaps/awards/pegram/index.cfm |title=George B. Pegram Award |work=APS Physics: SESAPS (home page) |accessdate=2008-06-10| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080705061925/http://www.aps.org/units/sesaps/awards/pegram/index.cfm| archivedate= 5 July 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

In 2008 the physics department announced the establishment of the Bascom S. Deaver Scholarship Fund, the first undergraduate scholarship program in physics at UVA, "in recognition of Prof. Deaver's great impact on [the UVA physics] program."<ref name="deaver-fund">{{cite web |url=http://www.phys.virginia.edu/Announcements/DeaverFund/ |title=Bascom S. Deaver Scholarship Fund |work=University of Virginia Department of Physics |accessdate=2008-06-06| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080615015716/http://www.phys.virginia.edu/Announcements/DeaverFund/| archivedate= 15 June 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

Deaver retired from academia in summer 2010, after 45 years at UVA.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Invitation - Deaver Retirement|url=http://www.phys.virginia.edu/Announcements/News/ViewPost.asp?UUID=6fb51f68-6b55-4a0a-b4d2-6d65dbab4f0f|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530170347/http://www.phys.virginia.edu/Announcements/News/ViewPost.asp?UUID=6fb51f68-6b55-4a0a-b4d2-6d65dbab4f0f |archive-date=2013-05-30 |access-date=2020-06-18|website=www.phys.virginia.edu}}</ref>
